summary: Phase 149O.20L.7L.3 -- Attack-Matrix Rows 33/34/36/37 and AST-Guard Multiline-Import Narrow Repair. FINAL VERDICT: NARROW REPAIR IMPLEMENTED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING. Repaired F-7L-5: rows 33, 34, 36, and 37 of HMIC-001 v1.4's attack matrix each carried a 'Not yet operative'/'production still computes the N-file/M-member set' claim, independently reconfirmed false against live production state (core/hatp_mandatory_certification.py's _FROZEN_AUTHORITY_BEARING_FILES has exactly thirty entries; derive_contract_versions returns exactly five members; both mechanically enforced since Phase 149O.20L.7K). Each row's caveat is repaired to 'Operative, not yet consequential', crediting the realignment while preserving each row's still-true 'no stored certification exists on this host' conclusion (independently confirmed: no certifications.json/certification-bindings.json/active-certification.json exists anywhere in the repository). Row 34's two additional false claims -- a hard-coded False readiness ceiling, and zero readiness/cutover callers of the certification validator -- were corrected: no literal `mandatory_consumption_implementation_independently_verified = False` assignment exists in hatp_mandatory_cutover.py (replaced by a dynamic call to validate_active_hatp_mandatory_independent_verification_certification at Phase 149O.19.5F, Wave F, commit 478f8b2c, independently confirmed ancestral to 149O.20L.7K via git log --oneline main); that validator has exactly one production caller outside its own definition site, confirmed by repository-wide grep. Row 37's own illustrative attack description was additionally corrected from a stale 'Version v1.0' to the live 'Version v1.1' (HBDC-001 has been v1.1 since Phase 149O.20L.7G). Row 38 and row 39, already repaired by 149O.20L.7L.1, are confirmed byte-unmodified. A whole-document stale-current-claim scan (beyond the four rows) found one further live, non-archival instance of the identical defect class: HMIC-REQ-145's own 'Status: CLOSED' closure paragraph stated in the present tense that its protection was 'not yet mechanically enforced in production' because the frozen-file constant 'still implements the pre-repair twenty-four-file set' -- repaired to state the closure is now mechanically enforced, since Phase 149O.20L.7K realigned that constant to the current thirty-file set. Every other 'hard-coded ceiling'/stale-count mention was independently read and classified: all live inside already-self-labeled 'descriptive/historical record of Phase 149O.XX' archival sections (accurate historical snapshots of that phase's own state, correctly left untouched, per this repository's own historical-truth-preservation discipline), or is normative SHALL/MUST requirement text (HMIC-REQ-114/HMIC-REQ-075, left unmodified per this phase's own STOP rule for normative-text changes), or a timeless attack-matrix illustration (row 4) -- none silently ignored. Repaired F-7L-7: the test-only AST-level `_pcae_imports` helper (tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_hmic_frozen_source_scope_amendment_independent_verification.py) recorded, for ast.ImportFrom, only node.module, never node.names, so `from pcae.core import hatp_deployment_binding_admin` (single- or multi-line, aliased or not) surfaced only 'pcae.core', never the producer's own dotted path -- independently reproduced against eleven literal ast.parse() adversarial snippets before any edit. A new, separate helper, `_pcae_import_targets`, was added alongside the byte-unchanged `_pcae_imports` (kept unchanged specifically because it also backs an unrelated, already-passing transitive-closure completeness check whose correctness depends on `_pcae_imports` returning only real module dotted names -- naively concatenating module.name for every ImportFrom alias there would have fabricated non-module strings, e.g. turning a genuine symbol import like HATPTrustStoreError into a fake ...hatp_bootstrap.HATPTrustStoreError 'module', and regressed that check). `_pcae_import_targets` additionally records module.name candidates for ImportFrom aliases -- the conservative package-vs-symbol adjudication required since Python's own grammar cannot statically disambiguate a submodule import from a symbol import without executing it (not attempted). A bare wildcard import is never silently treated as safe: it is surfaced in a dedicated second set the guard tests treat as suspicious. The two guard tests that previously called `_pcae_imports` for producer-reachability now call `_pcae_import_targets`: the primary unconditional AST guard, and the companion negative-direction check for hatp_mandatory_certification.py specifically (which carried the identical node.module-only gap in its own inline logic, also repaired). Full adversarial coverage (Import, ImportFrom, aliases, single- and multi-line, multiple names, module-vs-symbol adjudication, wildcard, and negative controls for path-string/comment/tuple-literal occurrences) is verified in the new tests/test_phase_149o_20l_7l_3_attack_matrix_and_ast_guard_narrow_repair.py (56 tests, all passing). Whole-tree reachability re-check confirms zero agent/runtime importers of the producer under src/pcae with the repaired guard; pyproject.toml's [project.scripts] block still exposes only the canonical `pcae` entry point, and cli.py references neither 'deployment_binding' nor the producer module name. The 149O.20L.7L.2 test module's own TestF7L5DeferredRowsCurrentlyFalse and TestASTGuardBlindSpot classes were updated in place, per that module's own original instruction to update rather than delete these guards once the gap they document closes. Two older, unrelated historical-phase test files (149O.19.5E.1, 149O.20D) pinned the now-superseded 'Not yet operative' wording as an expected literal substring; both were updated in place to assert the corrected 'Operative, not yet consequential' wording, with a comment documenting why. HMIC-001 remains v1.4 throughout -- same-version repair, mirroring section 52 (149O.20D.1), section 54 (149O.20L.1A), and section 56 (149O.20L.7L.1) precedent exactly. HMIC-REQ-052's three limbs are unchanged; only limb (c)'s already-corrected first-anchor prose and the four attack rows' descriptive caveats were touched. Regression evidence: full raw -m fast_green suite run in parallel on HEAD (pre-commit) and a disposable pre-repair git worktree at commit a1190b08 -- 278 vs 263 unique FAILED/ERROR node IDs pre-commit. Comm-diffed and independently classified every one of the fifteen 'new' node IDs: thirteen were working-tree-dirty self-checks (git status --porcelain / git diff --name-only HEAD against docs/contracts, from historical phases 149O.14/149O.19.5E.4/149O.1G/149O.20A/149O.20C(x2)/149O.20H/149O.20K.1/149O.20L.1/149O.20L.7D.9/149O.20L.7D.10/149O.20L.7D.11/149O.20L.7E), confirmed by direct code inspection to compare working tree against HEAD (not a fixed historical commit) and therefore expected to self-resolve on commit -- independently re-run after this phase's own implementation commit (85616f4b) and all thirteen now pass. Two were genuine content pins in unrelated historical-phase test files (149O.19.5E.1, 149O.20D) asserting the now-superseded stale 'Not yet operative' wording -- both updated in place and now pass. Post-commit full raw -m fast_green re-run: 263 unique FAILED/ERROR node IDs, identical count to the pre-repair baseline's 263 -- comm-diffed against the original baseline list, the only difference is a swap within the same pre-existing, already-documented order-dependent/subprocess-timeout shell_gate flake pair (test_verify_detects_tampered_record resolved, test_audit_verify_cli newly flaked on a 15-second CLI subprocess timeout, independently reproduced as a flake in isolation, unrelated to any file this phase touches). Deselected confirmation run (263-item deselect list, independently derived from the post-commit full raw run): 7551 passed, 0 failed, 5 skipped, run twice for stability, identical both times. Zero unexplained, zero content-related, zero security/authority/behavioral regressions. F-7L-5 (rows 33/34/36/37) and F-7L-7: REPAIRED -- INDEPENDENT VERIFICATION PENDING -- NOT CLOSED. F-7L-1/F-7L-2 remain CLOSED, untouched by this phase. 7J section 31 source-scope finding remains NOT CLOSED. Recommended next phase: 149O.20L.7L.4, an independent verification of this repair, before the 7J finding may close or first-use sequencing architecture may begin. HATP production remains NOT READY. Runtime remains Observed / observe / unavailable.
